parsed.explanation: The quote appears verbatim and, in context, is the write-up's only proposed Xiang strategy. It presupposes Liu's uniform marking at 1/(2n+1),...,(n)/(2n+1); marking the complementary grid points equalizes pieces only against that configuration. As a universal upper-bound strategy it fails: for n=1, if Liu marks 0.9 and Xiang marks 2/3, pieces are 2/3, 0.2333, 0.1, and Liu gets 2/3+0.1 ≈ 0.767 > 2/3. Checking the whole text, no upper bound over all Liu divisions is established anywhere: the write-up itself flags 'Upper bound: ... Strategy for X?' and 'Full proof (To be completed)'. Thus the objection correctly identifies that the universal upper-bound obligation is unmet (though the write-up honestly concedes this); the rubric credits only proven mechanisms, so the proof remains incomplete as written.
